stem: Which vesicoureteral reflux grade is associated with calyceal clubbing?
explanation: Grades 4 and 5 are associated with calyceal clubbing because reflux is severe enough to dilate and distort the renal calyces.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because grades 1 and 2 are limited to low-grade reflux and do not cause calyceal clubbing
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because grade 3 reflux reaches the renal pelvis but does not typically produce calyceal clubbing
optionExplanations.C: Correct because grades 4 and 5 represent high-grade reflux with dilatation and distortion of the calyces, producing calyceal clubbing
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because grade 1 only involves reflux into a non-dilated ureter and is the least severe form
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because calyceal clubbing is not present across all grades and is characteristic of the higher grades

source.hint: Recall which grades involve the highest pressure and most significant structural changes to the kidney.
